The story of Hubble. I will spend years just to have you back. Hubble was launched in 1990 to explore the universe and send us the pictures. But early images reveal the primary mirror was ground incorrectly by just two micrometers, causing blurry vision. That's the thickness of a hair strand. NASA was facing huge criticism from the government and people because of how expensive this project was. Everyone quit on Hubble but NASA determines the exact flaw and begins developing COSTAR (Corrective Optics Space Telescope Axial Replacement) and the Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 to act as glasses for the telescope. The STS-61 servicing mission deploys the Space Shuttle Endeavour. Over 11 days featuring five spacewalks, astronauts install the corrective optics, returning Hubble to its full potential. Fixing is always better than replacing. #space #EmotionalStory #wholesome #science
